raw.title: Software Engineering Manager (Hands-On, Frontend)
raw.description:
Join Pigment: The AI Platform Redefining Business Planning
 
Pigment is the AI-powered business planning and performance management platform built for agility and scale. We connect people, data, and processes in one intuitive, feature-rich solution, empowering every team - from Finance to HR - to build, adapt, and align strategic plans in real time.
 
Founded in 2019, Pigment is one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies globally. Industry leaders like Unilever, Uber, Anthropic, Snowflake or Siemens, use Pigment daily to make more informed decisions and confidently navigate any scenario.
 
With a team of 700+ across Paris, London, New York, Toronto, San Francisco and Austin, we've raised nearly $400M from top-tier investors and were named a Visionary in the 2024 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Financial Planning Software.
 
At Pigment, we take smart risks, celebrate bold ideas, and challenge the status quo - all while working as one team. If you're driven by innovation and ready to make an impact at scale, we’d love to hear from you.

We're hiring an Engineering Manager who wants to spend 80% of their time writing code, not attending management meetings.

About the role

Are you an experienced Software Engineer who loves writing code, solving complex technical problems and helping other engineers become better at what they do?

At Pigment, our Engineering Managers are engineers first.

Unlike traditional Engineering Manager positions, this role is designed for someone who wants to remain deeply involved in building software while taking on meaningful people-management responsibilities.

You'll spend approximately 80% of your time designing, coding and shipping production features, with the remaining 20% dedicated to coaching engineers, running regular 1:1s, providing feedback and supporting their development.

We're particularly interested in Senior Software Engineers who have naturally taken on coaching, mentoring or technical leadership responsibilities and are ready to develop further as people managers.

You don't necessarily need to have held an Engineering Manager title before. What matters most is your technical ability, your experience helping others grow and your motivation to combine engineering with people leadership.

You'll join Pigment's Reporting & Collaboration community, building sophisticated frontend experiences that help customers interact with complex data, configure workflows and make better business decisions.

 


What you'll do

🧑‍💻 Software Engineering (80%)

You'll remain an active contributor to our production codebase, working alongside other engineers on challenging frontend projects.

  • Write, review, refactor and ship production code regularly using React, TypeScript and JavaScript.

  • Design and build sophisticated user interfaces for interacting with large datasets, including filtering, visualisation and complex configuration.

  • Take ownership of engineering tasks and features from technical design through implementation, testing and deployment.

  • Solve challenging problems involving frontend performance, scalability, state management and user experience.

  • Participate in technical discussions, code reviews, debugging and architectural decisions.

  • Collaborate closely with Product Managers, Designers, Tech Leads and Software Engineers to deliver high-quality features.

  • Contribute to AI-powered product experiences and use modern development tools where appropriate.

  • Maintain the same technical expectations and engineering standards as our Senior Software Engineers.

    • You'll continue to write production code, not simply oversee the engineers who do.


    📚 Coaching & People Management (20%)

    Alongside your engineering responsibilities, you'll help other engineers develop their skills, confidence and careers.

    • Coach and mentor engineers, sharing technical knowledge and helping them improve their problem-solving abilities.

    • Hold regular 1:1 meetings with your direct reports to discuss progress, challenges and career development.

    • Provide constructive feedback, recognise achievements and support individual development plans.

    • Help engineers establish clear goals and understand the skills required to progress.

    • Support performance reviews and development discussions, including more challenging conversations when necessary.

    • Work alongside Tech Leads to understand engineers' technical contributions and development needs.

    • Help foster a collaborative engineering culture where people continuously learn from one another.

      • At Pigment, technical leadership and people management are intentionally separated. Tech Leads own the technical direction of teams, while Engineering Managers focus on coaching and developing engineers alongside their own coding responsibilities.

      You'll initially focus on contributing as a Senior Engineer before gradually taking on direct reports.


Who we're looking for

You're an engineer first, with a genuine interest in developing people.

  • You have substantial professional software-engineering experience and are technically operating at a strong Senior Engineer level.

  • You're currently hands-on with production code and want coding to remain the majority of your working week.

  • You have strong frontend development experience with React, TypeScript and JavaScript.

  • You've built complex, scalable applications, ideally within B2B SaaS, enterprise software, analytics or data-intensive environments.

  • You have experience coaching, mentoring or supporting other engineers through code reviews, pairing, technical discussions or structured feedback.

  • You enjoy sharing knowledge and helping other engineers improve.

  • You're interested in taking ownership of 1:1s, career development and people-management responsibilities, or already have experience doing so.

  • You're comfortable solving complex technical challenges independently while collaborating with others.

  • You care about product quality, engineering standards and delivering meaningful value to customers.

  • You're fluent in English. French is not required.

    • Previous formal people-management experience is a plus, but not a requirement. We're equally interested in strong Senior Engineers who have demonstrated the ability to coach others and are ready to take the next step.


Our interview process

Because Engineering Managers at Pigment spend approximately 80% of their time coding, they go through the same core technical assessments as our Software Engineers.

We want you to understand these expectations from the beginning.

1️⃣  Technical Screen

A technical discussion including a 15-minute code refactoring exercise.

AI assistance is not permitted during the refactoring exercise.

2️⃣  Live Coding

A hands-on algorithmic coding interview focused on problem-solving, code quality and technical reasoning.

AI assistance is not permitted.

3️⃣  System Design

A discussion exploring your approach to designing software systems, evaluating technical trade-offs and solving complex engineering problems.

4️⃣  Final Interview with the EML (Engineering Manager Lead)

A conversation exploring your motivation, engineering mindset, approach to coaching and alignment with Pigment's culture and expectations.

Important: Our Engineering Managers are assessed against the same senior technical engineering standards as our Software Engineers. This is a role for people who genuinely enjoy coding and want to keep doing it.


Is this role right for you?

You'll probably love this role if:

  • You enjoy writing code more than spending your day in management meetings.

  • You're a strong Senior Engineer who wants to help others grow.

  • You want to develop people-management skills without moving away from engineering.

  • You enjoy the challenge of balancing meaningful individual contributions with coaching responsibilities.

    • This probably isn't the right role if:

    • You're looking to move away from hands-on software development.

    • You prefer managing delivery, budgets and team strategy over building software.

    • You haven't written production code regularly for some time.

    • You're looking for a traditional Engineering Manager position where engineering work is mainly delegated to others.

      • At Pigment, you don't have to choose between being an excellent engineer and helping other engineers grow.


What you will get
  • Competitive salary
  • Equity
  • The best health insurance with Alan Blue is entirely free for you and your family 💙
  • Trust and flexible working hours
  • Brand new offices in the heart of Paris, London, New York, and, Toronto
  • Remote-friendly environment
    • We conduct background checks as part of our hiring process, in accordance with applicable laws and regulations in the countries where we operate. This may include verification of employment history, education, and, where legally permitted, criminal records. Any checks will be conducted lawfully prior to formal employment contracts being signed, with candidate consent, and information will be treated confidentially.
     
    Pigment is an equal opportunity employer. We believe diversity is a strength and fosters innovation. We are committed to enabling everyone to feel included and valued at the workplace.  All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, family, gender identity, marital status, national origin, physical or mental disability,  sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, social origin, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws. We may process your personal data in accordance with our HR Data Protection Notice.

raw.title: Senior/Principal Product Manager - Operations
raw.description:
About our team:

Radiant is redefining how AI infrastructure is built.

We design and operate AI-native infrastructure platforms engineered for sovereignty, performance, and scale — powering GPU-native workloads, multi-tenant control planes, and high-performance AI systems for the most demanding environments. We are building purpose-built AI infrastructure from powered land, to compute, to software.

As we scale our operations and deploy capital into the next generation of AI infrastructure, we are looking to expand our product team with leaders who can combine technical strength with execution excellence and are driven to build.

Radiant was established by Brookfield, a leading global alternative asset manager with over US$1 trillion of assets under management across real estate, infrastructure, renewable power and transition, private equity and credit. Brookfield's global relationships, investment expertise and access to long-term institutional capital provide Radiant with a differentiated platform from which to develop, finance and operate AI infrastructure assets. This combination of entrepreneurial execution and institutional sponsorship enables Radiant to pursue large-scale GPU and AI infrastructure opportunities globally.

Job Summary:

As a Senior Product Manager - Operations, you will own the strategy, roadmap, and delivery of Radiant’s internal tooling and integrations, helping teams operate and scale the cloud platform efficiently.

You’ll work across CMDB, asset and service inventory, internal APIs, workflow automation, third-party integrations, and platform administration, partnering closely with engineering, SRE, infrastructure, networking, security, and operations.

This is a highly technical product role focused on reducing operational friction, improving self-service, and creating reliable, scalable internal systems.

 

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own the strategy, roadmap, and delivery of internal tooling, CMDB, service catalogues, operational workflows, and integrations.

  • Translate business and operational needs into clear product requirements, specs, user stories, data models, and priorities.

  • Partner with engineering to define solutions across APIs, integrations, automation, and platform tooling.

  • Work with SRE, infrastructure, security, support, and other internal users to identify pain points and improve automation and self-service.

  • Establish reliable sources of truth for infrastructure, services, customers, environments, ownership, and configuration.

  • Drive prioritisation, backlog management, technical design discussions, delivery, and adoption.

  • Define success metrics and ensure tooling is secure, observable, auditable, reliable, and well documented.

  • Evaluate build vs. buy decisions and third-party tooling where appropriate.

Qualifications:

  • Experience owning technical products, internal platforms, developer tooling, or infrastructure products end-to-end.

  • Experience working across data centre operations, hardware lifecycle and inventory, infrastructure support, field operations, or adjacent operational environments.

  • Strong technical fluency across:

    • APIs & integrations: REST, gRPC, webhooks, third-party APIs

    • Infrastructure: Kubernetes, cloud platforms, containers, infrastructure-as-code

    • Data & CMDB: relational modelling, inventory, ownership, dependency mapping

    • Automation: queues, schedulers, workflow engines, event-driven systems

    • Observability & security: logging, metrics, tracing, IAM, RBAC, audit logging

  • Familiarity with tools such as NetBox, ServiceNow, Terraform, Grafana, Jira, or similar.

  • Strong understanding of distributed systems concepts including retries, idempotency, eventual consistency, and failure handling.

  • Strong prioritisation, communication, and stakeholder management skills.

  • Comfortable working closely with engineers and making informed technical trade-offs without needing to be the primary implementer.

  • Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment and taking ambiguous problems from discovery through to delivery.

What you bring:

  • Systems thinking: Understand how infrastructure, services, data, and operational workflows fit together.

  • Product thinking: Treat internal teams as customers and focus on measurable outcomes.

  • Technical fluency: Able to work credibly across APIs, integrations, infrastructure, data, and architecture.

  • Prioritisation: Balance operational pain, strategic value, technical complexity, and business impact.

  • Ownership: Drive ambiguous problems from discovery and definition through to adoption and iteration.

Our values:

  • Set the standard: Every single day, you spot opportunities to constructively shake things up

  • Inspire the change: There’s no blueprint for the future. You’ll embrace challenges and change

  • You’re real and you’re true to yourself: We cherish and celebrate diversity so you’ll feel right at home whoever you are and whoever you’re talking to, you treat everyone the same.

Why should you join us?

What sets us apart is our blend of modern technology, competitive benefits, and an open, welcoming work culture that enables our people to thrive.

Here are just some of the great things you can expect from us:

  • 25 days of annual leave

  • A culture that emphasises results over hierarchy, process & ego: we place great emphasis on the quality, ingenuity and creativity of work.

  • Open communication, regular feedback: we value smooth collaboration, direct and actionable feedback, and believe that leading with empathy and a growth mindset makes us better together.

  • Learning Time: we all have dedicated learning time to focus on new skills, projects or interests that lay outside of your day-to-day job.

  • Health & Wellbeing: we want everyone to feel healthy and happy, so we offer private medical insurance via Bupa.

  • Cycle to Work Scheme: we're committed to building a sustainable business, so we encourage cycling to work.

  • Gympass subscription to a variety of gyms and wellbeing apps

  • Participation in the company shares program

  • Enhanced parental pay & leave

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.


Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

About the role

You'll work alongside experienced engineers who will support you through code reviews, pairing and mentorship. We maintain a culture of ownership, and we value engineers who are curious about the business and keen to work with stakeholders to improve processes and the customer experience.

There are opportunities across platform engineering, B2B customer integration, conversion optimisation and business process automation. You'll work on a best-in class Open Banking decision-making platform and learn how to build systems that operate with low latency, at scale.

Python (including FastAPI, OpenTelemetry, procrastinate, SQLAlchemy, Uvicorn), Java,

React, Postgres, MySQL, Liquibase, Retool, Docker, AWS

  • Write clean, well-tested code in Python and Java, with guidance and feedback from senior engineers

  • Work with colleagues in Product and Design, as well as internal users, to understand requirements and turn them into working software

  • Help troubleshoot and resolve system issues that affect our customers, as part of a supported team rota during business hours

  • Write and improve SQL queries against our Postgres databases

  • Gradually take ownership of parts of the platform as your experience grows

  • Build and improve frontend features in React, and grow your skills across the full stack

Who you are

  • 0–2 years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent experience from a degree, bootcamp, internships or personal projects

  • Working knowledge of Java and Python – you don't need to be an expert, but you're comfortable writing and debugging code in both

  • Hands-on experience building frontend interfaces with React

How we work at Abound

To be successful here, our culture needs to energise you. Here is how we operate:

raw.description:
Why Faculty?


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here.

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

The Internal Communications Lead will build the machine and communications culture that keep Faculty's leadership and teams genuinely connected as we scale - carrying vision, strategy and our worldview on AI to every team undiluted, and surfacing the stories from across the business worth telling

This role has two core mandates:

1. Building the internal communications machine - you will design and own how leadership and our teams stay connected day to day - whether live or written, scheduled or ad hoc, and whatever formats a genuinely global, always-on business needs. You will build the architecture - cadence, ownership, structure - so the right message reaches the right people at the right moment, and noise becomes context rather than clutter.

2. Culture, Voice & Connection at Scale - you will be the person who makes sure leadership's vision, strategy and worldview on AI actually reach our teams everywhere, honest and crisp, without being diluted, delayed, or lost in translation as we grow. Leadership owns their voice and their point of view - that stays theirs. Your job is building the stage it's delivered from: sharp, timely, and sensitive to how a message lands differently across cultures and geographies.

What you own

  • The voice going down - The communications framework and rhythm that allow the Faculty Leadership to effectively communicate their vision, strategy and worldview on AI to every team, wherever they are in the world, undiluted and on time.

  • The voice from Accenture to Faculty - Point person for relevant Accenture news, updates and requirements that the Faculty teams need to know.

  • The detective work - Some of the best things happening at Faculty aren’t visible from the top. A team quietly solved a hard client problem. Someone's work never got the credit it deserved. A pattern of small wins nobody's connected into a story yet. You go looking for this, building the instincts and the relationships across the business to find the stories worth telling.

  • How we organise ourselves to communicate effectively - The architecture and judgment behind all of it so our people get a clear read of what matters without being buried under what doesn't.

What you will be doing

Forums & Formats

  • Design the company-wide forums that carry leadership's message, choosing the right format for the right moment rather than defaulting to habit

  • Build for global and cultural nuance from the start, so a message crafted in one office lands with the same weight and clarity in every other

  • Establish a working cadence that respects people's time and attention, so more communication is never mistaken for better communication

Channel Architecture & Cadence

  • Own the internal channel architecture, so messages reach the right people without adding to the volume everyone already wades through

  • Set clear ownership of who can broadcast to the whole company, on what, and how often

  • Bring judgement to every leadership message: which forum, format, tone and timing will make it land, and the confidence to say when something needs live delivery, a short note, or nothing broad at all

Storytelling & Culture

  • Play detective for the stories that don't naturally surface and give them the visibility they deserve

  • Treat culture preservation as a first-order responsibility of scale, not a side effect of good comms: building formats that carry how Faculty's leaders and teams work together, not just what the business is doing

Leadership & Collaboration

  • Where needed, partner closely with leadership as a trusted advisor, protecting their voice while making sure it travels well

  • Establish strong cross-functional relationships across regions and teams to understand what's really happening in the business and shape the internal communications programme around it

  • Support the international expansion of Faculty's internal communications, working with regional colleagues to ensure forums and formats travel well and adapt where they need to

What we are looking for

  • Designing the Machine - A track record of designing and building the machine from scratch - cadences, channels, and company-wide forums - rather than simply running an existing playbook.

  • Judgement - A sharp instinct for signal versus noise: what deserves broad visibility, what doesn't, and the confidence to say so to senior stakeholders.

  • Storytelling - A detective's instinct for finding the story in a large, fast-moving organisation, and the ability to tell it with clarity and a genuine point of view.

  • Global & Cultural Fluency - Proven experience communicating across geographies and time zones, with real sensitivity to how messages land differently across cultures and offices.

  • Stakeholder Management - Skilled at working alongside senior leaders and founders, earning trust quickly through sound judgement and discretion.

  • Communication - Exceptional written and verbal skills, able to convey a complex or nuanced leadership message clearly and briefly without losing what made it worth saying.

  • Change & Scale Experience - Experience communicating through a period of fast growth, acquisition, or significant organisational change, ideally in a technical or fast-moving industry.

  • Autonomy & Resilience - Highly self-sufficient, with the flexibility and tenacity to thrive in a fast-paced, complex scale-up environment now operating at global scale.

Our Interview Process

  1. Talent Team Screen (30mins)

  2. Introduction with the Hiring Manager (60 mins)

  3. Panel Interview involving pre work (75 mins)

Our Recruitment Ethos

We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.

If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours.

A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

raw.title: Senior SecOps Engineer
raw.description:
What is Flagstone?

Flagstone is many things. An online savings platform, reinventing how individuals, businesses, and charities manage, protect, and grow their cash. A diverse group of people, bound by a collaborative spirit, and shared purpose. And lastly, a thriving, profitable business – where smart people do their best work.

Each definition shares a common thread: our unique culture. It’s our pride and joy. And our competitive advantage.

A feel for our culture:

To revolutionise the savings market, we need to be at our best. But high performance takes more than talent – it takes a culture of kindness, respect, and growth.

That’s why we’re building a diverse, inclusive community, where your voice is heard and valued. Where, with close support and room to develop, you can surpass even your own expectations. And be rewarded for it.

We may not change the world, but we can change the world of financial technology. And all it takes is a winning mix of drive, talent, and empathy. Our culture celebrates all three.

But enough about us. Let’s talk about you.

About the role

We’re looking for a Senior SecOps Engineer to take ownership of security operations at Flagstone. That covers everything from alert triage and incident response through to detection engineering and continuous improvement of how our SOC works.

This is a hands-on role that sits right at the operational end of security. You’ll spend real time in the alert queue, as well as building the detections and automation that make it better. You’ll be right in the middle of complex investigations and P1s, while also shaping how the function operates. You’ll also own our relationship with our managed SOC provider, setting the standards they work to rather than simply receiving their output.

About the team

You’ll sit within Security Engineering, reporting to our Security Team Leader. In this role you’ll own detection, triage and incident response, and act as the technical counterpart to our managed SOC provider. That means directing their scope, holding them to clear detection and response standards, and keeping ownership of anything escalated or high severity in house.

Does this sound like you?

You’re an engineer at heart. You’d rather write the detection than describe it, and you treat detections and automation like any other engineering work: version controlled, tested and documented. You’re the go to expert when something serious happens, and you can explain security risk just as clearly to engineers as to senior stakeholders.

You’re curious about new technology, AI included, and you have a clear view on where it genuinely helps and where it introduces risk.

What you’ll do

You’ll take ownership of our SOC operations and report on their performance and health to stakeholders across the business. You’ll run investigations and incident response for complex or high severity alerts, managing parallel workstreams, keeping stakeholders informed and running post incident reviews through to real changes in detections or process.

You’ll own the detection engineering backlog, building, tuning and retiring detections across Microsoft Sentinel and Defender, mapped to a coverage model such as MITRE ATT&CK. You’ll turn threat intelligence into detection logic and hunting activity, and drive our automation and SOAR maturity by building Logic App playbooks that reduce manual effort without losing judgement on the nuanced cases.

You’ll manage our managed SOC relationship day to day: defining scope and escalation criteria, reviewing performance against SLAs and acting as the technical escalation point for anything they can’t close. You’ll keep playbooks, escalation paths and documentation in shape so the practice scales beyond any one person, and you’ll track metrics like triage time, false positive rate and coverage gaps to drive continuous improvement.

You’ll also explore and introduce AI assisted tooling into SOC workflows, such as triage and enrichment copilots, detection authoring and alert summarisation, where it clearly makes a difference, with sensible boundaries on where human judgement stays in the loop.

What you’ll bring

  • 5+ years in a SOC, security operations or detection engineering role, with progression into a senior IC position

  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft Sentinel and Defender, building detections rather than just consuming alerts

  • Experience running investigations and incident response, including communicating with stakeholders under pressure

  • Experience building SOAR and automation content (for example Sentinel Logic Apps), including monitoring for silent failure

  • A strong grasp of attack patterns and MITRE ATT&CK, and how to turn them into a detection coverage model

  • Experience directing a managed or outsourced SOC or MDR provider, setting scope, SLAs and escalation criteria

  • Practical experience applying AI or LLM tooling to SecOps work

  • Strong communication and stakeholder skills, with the confidence to influence senior stakeholders

  • Critical thinking and a real curiosity for new technologies and frameworks

It would be great if you also have

  • Experience in regulated financial services

  • Exposure to identity centric detection (Entra ID) and cloud native threat detection

  • GCIH, GCFA or an equivalent hands-on IR or detection certification

  • Links to the SOC and detection engineering community, through conferences, speaking or open source detection content such as Sigma rules

How we reward you:

At Flagstone, the benefits extend beyond false gifts like “fruit and snacks”. Instead, we invest in your health, wealth, and professional development. Here’s a selection of our benefits:

  • Hybrid working - Spend at least 1 day a week with your team in our collaborative London office

  • Competitive bonus scheme - designed to reward and recognise high performance

  • Flexible benefits budget - a pot to fund meaningful benefits for you, whether it's hormone or fertility testing, cancer screening, neuro-diversity coaching or something that matters for you.

  • A range of salary sacrifice options to help you make tax efficient savings on electric cars, nursery schemes, home and tech goods.

  • Around the World scheme - 3 months work from anywhere scheme

  • Mental wellbeing support – Access therapy and mental health sessions through Spill

  • Learning and development – £1,000 personal development budget to help you grow in your role.

  • Private health care - Enjoy all the benefits AXA has to offer, including reduced gym memberships and medical history disregarded

  • Medical cash plan - To help you with the costs of dental and optical expenses

  • Life insurance and Income Protection- four times your annual salary for peace of mind

  • Matched pension contributions up to 5%

  • 25 days holiday - plus bank holidays, well-being days and volunteering days

  • Enhanced Parental Leave – enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption pay.  

All are welcome.

At Flagstone, we’re assembling a diverse team that defies our industry’s norms. Think this role could suit you? We encourage you to apply, no matter your background.

raw.description:
About Griffin

Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.

We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.

We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.

Learn more about what we do

Our culture

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture.

The Team

The Craft function has seven small, cross-functional engineering teams - each with engineers, an engineering manager, and a product manager, working closely with designers.

You will work across the whole Craft function, with the remit of improving our controls and cyber security governance. You will initially work with and report to the Engineering Manager for Infrastructure as you establish yourself and take on your day to day responsibilities, additionally you will work closely with our CTO and Founder, Allen Rohner.

The Opportunity

We're looking for an Engineer 1.5 to become the engineering voice of security, compliance and assurance at Griffin. Sitting across engineering, security, risk and operational resilience, you'll turn standards and regulatory expectations into practical controls that engineers actually want to use and you’ll build those controls yourself, shipping code to production alongside the engineering team. You’ll also give our second and third lines real confidence in what we’ve built. It’s a rare hybrid role with broad ownership and a direct hand in strengthening Griffin’s security.

What Success Looks Like

In your first 6 months, you'll have taken ownership of our certification, attestation and audit work including ISO 27001 and SWIFT, with evidence organised and findings driven through to closure. Our engineering risks and controls will be well maintained, and our release, change and post-incident processes will be stronger. You’ll have shipped code that automates control checks and evidence collection, and you’ll be a regular contributor to our codebase.

By month 12 our resilience plans, including Important Business Service technical mapping, B& Continuity Planning and disaster recovery, will be current, and security and compliance will be easier to run and easier to demonstrate to customers, thanks to clearer ownership and smart automation.

To Do This You’ll Own

  • Control design and cyber security governance: translating standards into practical engineering controls and building and shipping the code that puts them in place, working with Engineering teams to get them live

  • Certifications and attestations, from SWIFT and FPS today to schemes like SOC 2 and ISO 27001 in the future, including the documentation behind them

  • Internal and external audits and customer due diligence requests, owning findings and driving them to closure

  • Engineering Risk and Controls Self Assessments, controls and actions, plus recurring control activity such as chaos testing and backup/restore

  • Code release and change management, improving the process and sampling releases to check adherence to policy

  • Post-incident reviews, including follow-up actions and sharing learnings with the right stakeholders

  • Engineering's contribution to operational resilience (DR plans and IBS technical mapping) and to managing engineering third parties alongside Operations

We expect you to shape this role

This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves—that's for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are.

Your background

To ensure this, we're looking for people who have:

  • A hands-on engineering or technical background, including experience writing and shipping production code with an engineering-first approach to turning standards into practical controls and technical delivery

  • Experience in security, compliance, risk or assurance within a technical environment, including owning or significantly contributing to audits, certifications or attestations

  • Strong knowledge of compliance, risk and cyber security principles, and a broad understanding of change and release management, incident management, operational resilience and third-party governance

  • Sharp analytical and assurance skills: spotting gaps, assessing adherence to standards and following actions through

  • Stakeholder management and influencing skills across Engineering, SMEs, auditors and control functions, with a pragmatic, proportionate approach to governance

  • A love of writing - we have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write)

Ideally, you would also:

  • Be familiar with frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, SWIFT and FPS, ideally from a regulated fintech or challenger bank environment

  • Have used automation and code to improve security, compliance or control processes and documentation

What can we offer you?

We are an early stage startup and we're working hard to expand our benefits package. We're planning to add to this list in the future.

  • Remote-first flexibility: Work from anywhere in the UK

  • Work from abroad: Up to 20 days a year

  • Time off: 25 days’ holiday, bank holidays and a winter break (we shut down between Christmas and New Year)

  • Share options: Own a part of what we’re building together

  • Pension: Auto-enrolment into our Penfold scheme

  • Insurance: Private medical with Bupa (including family cover) and life insurance with AIG

  • Wellbeing: 1:1 coaching and therapy session available through Oliva

  • Family leave: Enhanced parental leave with up to 6 months on full pay after two years’ service

  • AI tools: Everyone has a Claude subscription on us and access to other premium tools

  • Your setup: We’ll support you in creating a comfortable and effective WFH environment.

As a bank, we’re committed to maintaining the highest standards of security. This means that the successful candidate will need to complete background screening, and our offer will be conditional upon satisfactory review of these checks. This would include verification of right to work, criminal record, credit history, social media and professional reference checks.

 

How do I apply?

Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next.

We’re remote-first

We trust people to do great work wherever they are. We hire across the UK and most of our team works remotely full-time. We have a small London office in Moorgate for those who want it, and about a third of the company is close enough to use it occasionally, but there's no expectation to be there. What matters is the work, not where you do it.

Under representation

At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance

Griffin Bank Ltd request that recruitment agencies do not speculatively submit CVs to any employee or associate of our company unless explicitly asked to do so by a member of our Talent team.

Any CVs sent to any member of our team on a speculative basis will not be recognised and we will not accept liability for any fee or commission should we subsequently employ a candidate who applied to us directly or was introduced by an instructed agency that may also have been submitted speculatively by an uninstructed agency.

TL;DR

Millions of people build on Lovable, from software that runs new businesses to the tools that power existing ones. At the center of it all is trust. That’s why we’re looking for an exceptional storyteller to spearhead Lovable’s trust, safety, and security communications efforts.

Why Lovable

For decades, the ability to build software belonged to a tiny fraction of the population: the people with the credentials, the technical training, the access. Everyone else had to wait, or pay, or give up. Lovable is the counterargument: We exist for the people with ideas who were locked out of software creation until now.

Over 70 million projects have been built on the platform. Hundreds of thousands of people pay for it. The product handles real infrastructure, not only prototypes: authentication, databases, payments, and deployment. People run real businesses on Lovable, which means the stakes are real too.

The comms challenge: when anyone can build, the platform has to be safe for everyone who does, and they need to know it. That takes someone who can tell the story of how we think about topics like safety, security, and reliability before anyone asks, and who can be honest, precise, and fast when the questions come up anyway.

What you’ll do

Build and own Lovable’s trust narrative. You’ll own Lovable’s trust narrative in earned, new, and owned media, proactively telling the story of how we think about security, privacy, and safety. You’ll shape the stories that highlight our commitments and ensure we show up in the conversations where trust in AI platforms is being decided right now.

Be the comms partner to our security and trust leadership. You’ll develop and own the spokesperson platforms for our CISO and other senior leaders who speak on our trust efforts, identifying and preparing them for on-stage and media opportunities. You’ll help them become recognized voices on topics of trust in AI software creation.

Own incident communications, end to end. When something doesn’t go as planned, you’re the incident comms lead who ensures clear and swift communications for every audience that needs to hear from us, including media, customers, and employees. You’ll build and run the playbook that lets us move faster each time.

Build relationships with relevant media and creators. You’ll know the voices who matter most in telling our trust story, and you’ll make sure those relationships exist before we need them.

Who you are

You’ve done trust, safety, or security communications. You have proven comms experience across a variety of trust-related topics, from AI safety to security. You’ve worked on or alongside security, privacy, or trust and safety teams.

You have real incident experience. You’ve been the incident comms lead more than once, and you’ve probably written a playbook along the way. You bring the attention to detail, precision, speed, and judgment an incident requires.

You have strong media relationships in the tech and AI ecosystem. Security and trust reporters, analysts, policy-adjacent media, perhaps even researchers. You know who they are, what they care about, and how to earn their attention honestly.

You’re voraciously curious. You don’t need to be an engineer, but you need to be willing to understand how a platform like ours works well enough to describe an incident accurately and explain a safety decision without hand-waving.

You write clearly and have keen attention to detail. Your writing is precise, human, and accessible, even when the subject matter is complex or the situation is sensitive. You also catch things others may miss.

You’re calm, hands-on, and low-ego. You’ll draft the statements, build the media list, prep the spokesperson, and coordinate across teams yourself. You thrive in environments where the plan often changes and the pace is relentless.

You have 6+ years of experience in communications, with significant time spent on trust and safety, security, or incident communications at a technology company. We care more about the right years than the number of them: judgment under pressure matters more than tenure.

What you need to know

This is a strategic but hands-on role with both proactive and reactive components. That means you’ll need to be comfortable being the person who’s on call when something breaks, while simultaneously leading the charge on work that moves our trust narrative forward. The role itself lives at the intersection of several functions, and you’ll be the one finding the red thread among all that’s happening so we can tell a cohesive story externally.

Lovable is a European company with a global audience. The trust story has to resonate outside of Silicon Valley and our home turf in Stockholm. Wherever you sit, you’ll work across time zones and build relationships with the teams whose work you’re talking about.

Finally: joining Lovable Comms means you’re deeply curious, data-driven, and not extremely precious about role boundaries. You find ways to work smarter with AI, to measure what matters, and to step into work that isn’t technically “yours” when the moment calls for it.

Real estate shapes the world around us: our homes, our workplaces and our cultural landmarks. It’s the infrastructure that powers everyday life and is the world's largest asset class. Here, you'll be part of changing how the deals behind the largest asset class get transacted, and will help shape the future of real estate.

A bit about us:

🚀 We’re building at the forefront of AI technology, without losing the deeply human expertise our clients depend on.

🏢 Orbital is built with former practising real estate lawyers and 250+ years of combined legal expertise. We're purpose-built for the complexity of real estate: accelerating due diligence, drafting and negotiation, and deal coordination with legal-grade precision.

💰 We've just raised a $60m Series B, led by Brighton Park Capital, to accelerate our global expansion – $75m raised to date.

🤝 We're trusted by 5,000+ real estate professionals, spanning UK Magic Circle and US Am Law 100 firms, to household names like M&S. Leading firms like BCLP, Orrick, Goodwin, Womble Bond Dickinson and Clifford Chance rely on Orbital to remove the busywork, freeing legal and real estate teams to focus on sharp judgment, standout client service, and closing deals faster.

💡 Working at Orbital means joining a bold, ambitious team, with the trust to take ownership and make a real impact from day one.

The role

You will report directly to the CTO and work alongside engineering, product, legal engineering and AI from the start. Your direct team is small today, three designers, and you will shape how it grows from here.

Your starting point is not a design backlog handed to you in advance. It is the product strategy, growth ambition, and AI-first operating model, and you will use that context to set the design agenda.

Orbital is at an inflection point. The product is live and trusted by some of the most demanding real estate legal professionals in the world. The challenge now is not building something from scratch but making it significantly better: cleaner, faster, and genuinely easier to trust. As the product scales across the UK and US, the design function needs to grow with it, and you will be the person who builds it.

What you'll do

Lead from the product.

Your first team is the product engineering leadership team. You will be part of product, commercial, and strategic conversations, bringing a strategic design perspective to business challenges rather than representing the design function in isolation. From there, you will form your own view on where the product experience is constraining growth, where the interface is creating friction for users, and what needs to change. You will help the leadership team pressure-test product decisions against user reality, spot where information architecture, interaction patterns, or visual clarity are becoming bottlenecks, and ensure that how we design is aligned with where the business is heading.

Set the design agenda from product context.

You will not be given a predefined project list. You will assess what you learn from the product, the users, and the business and set the design priorities from there. That means making sure areas like information architecture, interaction design, design systems, user research, and AI interface patterns are pointed at the right problems and prioritised accordingly. A major part of the brief is translating current product realities into a sharper design mandate and challenging existing assumptions when the evidence demands it.

Define what AI-native design looks like here.

The hardest design problems at Orbital are not aesthetic. They are epistemic. How do you help a real estate lawyer trust an AI output enough to put their name to it? How do you present the reasoning behind a 50-document analysis in a way that a partner can review in 20 minutes? How do you make agentic behaviour feel controllable to a professional who is accountable for the outcome? You will set the standard for how Orbital answers those questions, shape the interaction patterns that distinguish our product from everything else in the market, and hold the wider team accountable for the quality of the experience we ship.

Build the design function.

You will be the consistent presence the design team anchors around. You will invest in their growth, develop clear ownership within the function, and be accountable for the team's development over time, not just its immediate output. Over time you will shape a high-leverage design function that combines strong craft, deep user understanding, and a genuine instinct for where AI changes the rules.

Requirements

The must-haves

  • Significant experience leading product design at a senior level at a scaling B2B tech company. You bring real depth across the design discipline. That foundation is essential, but what sets you apart is the ability to operate beyond it.

  • A track record of sitting at the product leadership table and influencing business decisions, not just delivering a design agenda within one.

  • Experience scaling a design function through a high-growth phase, with the judgment to know what process and structure matters at each stage and what slows you down.

  • You have designed AI-native products. Not tools with AI bolted on. You have worked through the real problems: explainability, trust, agentic UX, confidence signals. You have opinions formed from real experience.

  • You have designed for expert professional users, people who know their domain better than any designer ever will, and you understand how to design for that dynamic without condescending or oversimplifying.

  • Strong commercial instincts. You understand how product design affects adoption, retention, and revenue, and you can connect design decisions to business outcomes.

  • The ability to translate product context into a design strategy and challenge existing priorities when the evidence demands it.

  • Experience leading through a design team, setting direction and standards without owning every deliverable.

And a few nice-to-haves

  • Direct experience of a Series B to Series C growth journey.

  • Built a design function from an early-stage base rather than inherited one.

  • Familiarity with legal tech, fintech, compliance tech or another domain where precision and professional accountability shape every design decision.

  • Experience building or significantly evolving a design system that improved team velocity at scale.

Why you'll love it here

  • You will join a company at a genuine inflection point, with real influence at the product engineering leadership table from day one.

  • You will shape the design function rather than inherit one, with room to build it around craft, research, and AI-first thinking.

  • The design problems here are some of the most interesting and challenging in the market.

  • You will be part of a collaborative, highly ambitious team where the standard is high and the ownership is real.

Benefits 🌟

🧑 💻 We believe in flexibility, but we're also big on in-person collaboration. This role is based in our London office with an expectation of multiple days in the office per week. It's about being present when it matters, and balancing autonomy with commitment.

🏢 Equity options in a fast-growing startup

🌴 25 days holiday plus bank holidays

📚 Personal development budget and learning opportunities

🍔 Free lunch on Wednesdays and Deliveroo budget for late nights

🚲 Cycle-to-work scheme

📚 A bias toward experimentation, rapid learning, and iterating quickly based on real feedback

We're in the process of building an inclusive, welcoming culture where everyone feels seen and valued. Expect regular team off-sites, shared lunches, and social events, with something for everyone.

🔒 Security is everyone’s responsibility at Orbital. We ask all team members to follow our security policies, complete regular awareness training, and handle sensitive data with care in line with ISO 27001 standards. Spot something unusual? Reporting risks or incidents quickly helps us maintain the strong culture of security and compliance we all depend on.

raw.description:
About Plasma

Plasma is building the primary account for global money.

Money used to belong to a country. Increasingly, it belongs to a person or business moving through many countries. People and businesses now earn, spend, save, hire and invest across borders. Traditional banks cannot serve this new world.

Our first product, Plasma One, is a global money account: a place to receive, hold, send funds in seconds, earn yield and spend with a card in the local economy.

Underneath is the Plasma network, built from first principles for stablecoin payments. Stablecoins make dollars faster, cheaper and more reliable to move.

The opportunity is to become where all global money lands first: where income arrives, balances grow, payments move, businesses operate, and new financial products are built.


The Team & Our Story

We are a global team of founders, operators and engineers, obsessed with building the best products. We work at the cutting edge of financial innovation, using stablecoins to create tools for consumers and businesses.

We operate with trust, clarity, and ambition: own your craft, move with urgency, contribute beyond your lane, back your teammates, debate rigorously, and keep raising the bar for what great means.

Customer Experience

Plasma is scaling its customer-facing operations across international markets, and we’re growing the Customer Experience Team to match. You’ll join an established team and take ownership of coverage for the CET time zone, making sure our customers get great support when they need it most.

You’ll work across the full customer journey, from first contact through to resolution. Because we’re still building out our playbook, your input will directly shape the processes, standards, and team culture as we grow. You won’t just follow the process; you’ll help refine it.

Some flexibility in working hours & weekend shifts will be needed to support coverage and the occasional busy period. We’re looking for a hard-working self-starter who thrives in a fast-moving startup environment and is committed to the mission alongside the rest of the team.

The role

  • Own the customer experience day-to-day: Be the first person our customers reach when something goes wrong or they need help. You will handle inbound queries across chat, email, and support tooling, and take accountability for the quality and speed of every response.

  • Be the right hand of the Ops lead: Work directly alongside the Head of Operations to build out processes, identify gaps, and support decisions as we scale the team internationally. This is not a back-office support role. You will be involved in how we think about operations.

  • Build the foundations: We are early. Many of the processes, templates, and escalation paths do not exist yet. You will create them. From response frameworks to internal guides, you will help lay the groundwork the team will rely on as we grow.

  • Support international team scaling: As we hire Ops team members in new markets, you will help onboard them, share knowledge, and maintain consistency in how we deliver for customers across regions.

  • Spot problems before they become patterns: Track issues across the customer base, flag recurring themes to Product and Engineering, and help prioritise fixes that actually move the needle for customers.

  • Work across teams: Collaborate with Compliance, KYC, and Product to make sure the customer experience is joined up, especially during onboarding and verification flows where things can go wrong quickly.

  • Represent the customer internally: Your proximity to customer feedback is valuable. Use it. Bring customer insight into internal conversations and push for improvements that matter.

  • Be Flexible with Shift Rotation: Most weeks you’ll work the normal Mon-Fri, however team members currently rotate weekend shifts which means that you may be required to work a weekend shift once every 6 weeks. You’ll then be able to take those days worked off the following week.

The Bar

  • 1 to 3 years of experience in customer operations, customer success, or a support role, ideally within fintech, payments, or crypto. We will consider strong candidates from outside these sectors if the fit is right.

  • Someone who takes ownership. You do not wait to be told. When something is broken or missing, you fix it or flag it. You hold yourself to a high standard even when no one is watching.

  • Clear and direct in how you communicate. You can write a helpful, professional response under pressure and explain a complex situation simply. You know the difference between being thorough and overcomplicating things.

  • Competent English Language - our team communicates in english so being competent with the language is a requirement.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity. This is an early-stage company. Processes will change, priorities will shift, and some days you will be figuring things out as you go. You see that as interesting rather than frustrating. Preferably, you have worked at a fast-paced tech company.

  • Genuinely curious about crypto. You do not need deep technical knowledge, but you need to understand the basics of how stablecoins and digital assets work and be motivated to learn more. Our customers live in this space.

  • Organised under pressure. You can manage a queue, prioritise effectively, and keep quality high when things are busy.

  • Collaborative by default. You work well with people in different functions, different time zones, and different levels of seniority. Building the team abroad means working with people you may never meet in person, and you are good at that.

Nice to have

  • Experience in a startup or scale-up where you had to build or rebuild processes, not just follow them.

  • Exposure to Intercom, Zendesk, Freshdesk, or similar support tooling in a live production environment.

  • Any familiarity with KYC or compliance workflows as they relate to customer onboarding.

  • Experience supporting or managing a small team, even informally, or helping onboard new colleagues.

  • An interest in how stablecoin and DeFi products work and the customer challenges they create.

  • Multilingual skills that could support customer communication across our international markets.

What's in it for you

  • Above-market salary for the level of the role, with token compensation.

  • A beautiful London HQ with gym access and daily food, for those who thrive in an office environment. Visa sponsorship and relocation support if you're joining from abroad.

  • Premium health insurance for you and your family, fully covered by Plasma.

  • Monthly wellness budget, whether that's the gym, therapy, sauna, or massage.

  • All the tools and tech you need to operate at your best.

  • Real ownership and responsibility from day one, with your work shipping to hundreds of thousands of people, moving millions of dollars every day.

Data Protection & Privacy
We are committed to protecting the privacy and security of your personal data. Any personal information you provide during the recruitment process will be processed in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable local data protection laws.

Scarlet is authorised to assess and certify medical devices. We combine clinical, technical and regulatory expertise with AI agents and software so rigorous certification can keep pace with product development at the world’s most ambitious technology companies, without lowering the safety bar.

Our customers have cut a year or more from their certification timelines for new AI-enabled medical devices and shortened product-update cycles from months to weeks. You’ll join a team building the infrastructure that makes these outcomes repeatable at scale.

About the role

As a Certification Program Manager at Scarlet, you will help safe medical technologies reach patients sooner by running and improving the operations behind their certification.

You will own operational delivery across customer certification programs, working closely with auditors, assessors and account managers. This is a hands-on role: delivering detailed work accurately and on time, while finding ways to make certification simpler and more efficient.

As Scarlet expands into new markets and jurisdictions, you will help shape the processes that support that growth. You’ll build expertise across a varied range of certification activities, with scope to take ownership of broader operational improvements.

  • Streamline certificate transfers by coordinating next steps with customers and outgoing certification bodies.

  • Triage medical device change notifications and coordinate the appropriate specialist review, improving how changes are categorised and routed.

  • Keep customers and colleagues informed of progress, outstanding actions and next steps.

  • Work with product and engineering to improve procedures and automate routine workflows, so your work increasingly focuses on the most complex customers and cases.

Required qualifications

  • Evidence of solving difficult problems independently. You can explain an unfamiliar problem you tackled, how you broke it down, the decisions you made and the result you achieved.

  • An eye for detail. Experience reviewing detailed documents or data for completeness and accuracy.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience in healthcare, certification or another regulated industry.

  • Knowledge of medical technology and the role of certification.

Your next adventure awaits!

Join the team who are redefining the payments space.

About Us

At Vitesse, we're more than just a payments platform – we're the trusted financial infrastructure connecting the global insurance ecosystem. Tailor-made for insurers, brokers, MGAs, and TPAs, our unified platform optimises claims funds, enables real-time global payments, and delivers full financial control. Our impact is real: over $20 billion in payments across 200+ countries, hundreds of millions returned to insurers’ balance sheets, and counting. We’re licensed in the UK (FCA), Europe (DNB), and New York (NYDFS), with over 260 amazing colleagues worldwide. With $93 million recently raised in Series C funding from KKR, our journey is just beginning, and our ambitions are sky-high.

Headquartered in the heart of London and expanding across Europe and the US, Vitesse is where your ideas power tomorrow’s insurance solutions. Are you ready to make a difference? You're in the right place.

Customer Success at Vitesse is still taking shape, which means if you join us you’ll have a genuine opportunity to shape how the function works – from engagement models and playbooks, to the way we measure customer value and growth. You’ll be responsible for our enterprise customer sucesss team that owns a portfolio of our Vitesse’s largest and most complex customers across the carrier, TPA and MGA market. These matrixed organisations often have multiple stakeholder groups, complex operating models and legacy systems. You’ll help the team navigate that complexity, build trusted executive relationships and grow the value customers realise from Vitesse. Your ideas will matter, and your impact will be visible.

The Role

Reporting into the VP of Customer Success, you’ll lead a team of CSMs and personally own one or two strategic accounts. Together, you’ll drive material growth across our Enterprise customer base by helping customers realise measurable value and increase their use of Vitesse

You’ll guide the team to build strong relationships, from operational users to senior executives, and mobilise the right people across Vitesse to deliver on customer priorities. Strong adoption and customer health will underpin that growth. You’ll work closely with Sales, Pre-Sales, Product, Onboarding, Operations, Support and Data to make it happen.

Core Responsibilities

  • Coach and develop Enterprise CSMs to act as trusted advisers and build effective relationships with senior customer stakeholders.

  • Guide the team in creating and delivering Customer Success Plans that connect customer goals to Vitesse’s value, with clear success measures, regular check-ins and strategic reviews.

  • Hold the team accountable for customer outcomes, portfolio health and growth in balances, payment accounts, participant connections and Vitesse’s share of payment activity.

  • Help CSMs map stakeholder groups, identify risks early and coordinate action across customer and internal teams.

  • Guide the team through complex customer initiatives by clarifying ownership, aligning stakeholders and keeping activity focused on agreed outcomes.

  • Support customers in enabling third parties in their payment networks, coordinating across CSMs and other internal teams where needed.

  • Partner with Sales to identify and qualify expansion opportunities.

  • Bring customer feedback to Product and operational teams, and shape the Enterprise Customer Success model and practices.

Why Join Us?

Vitesse is a high-growth business with a strong, open and positive culture. We combine the innovative energy of a scale-up with proven product-market fit and a significant market opportunity.

As Customer Success Lead, Enterprise, you’ll shape how we work with some of our largest customers, lead a talented team and help build an approach suited to complex organisations and meaningful growth.

Skills and Experience

  • Experience leading and developing a Customer Success or Account Management team in insurance or a complex B2B technology environment.

  • Experience managing strategic accounts with matrixed organisations and multiple operational, technical and executive stakeholders.

  • A record of helping customers realise measurable value and growing adoption or usage within existing relationships.

  • Confidence coaching teams to engage senior executives and communicate business value.

  • Strong commercial judgement and the ability to turn customer insight into credible account and growth plans.

  • The ability to guide teams through complex customer initiatives, keeping outcomes, ownership and risks clear.

  • Strong cross-functional leadership and knowledge of carriers, TPAs, MGAs or the wider insurance ecosystem, or the ability to build that expertise quickly.

  • An adaptable leadership style and interest in shaping an evolving Enterprise Customer Success model.

We understand that everyone has their own work rhythm and believe in a flexible working schedule - at Vitesse you’re expected to work 35 hours a week.

The Vitesse values are a true reflection of what it takes to thrive in our business, so it’s important to us that any employee who joins our business is aligned with these 3 attributes

Confident Humility
We believe the best ideas come from listening and learning. We leave ego at the door, ask for help when we need it, and celebrate collective success. When one of us wins, we all do.

Driven to Succeed
We’re ambitious about the opportunity ahead and committed to achieving it together. We hold ourselves to high standards, take pride in what we deliver, and push for meaningful outcomes for our customers, our partners, and each other.

Tenacious Responsibility
We take ownership of our work, our decisions, and our results. We face challenges with resilience, learn from setbacks, and see things through to completion. Because doing the right thing matters.

Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. You’re willing to roll your sleeves up and go deep with prospective customers on their functional and technical needs, partnering with our sales, product and climate science teams along the way. You may be a carbon accounting aficionado or you may have never worked in climate before but have a passion for the subject; either way, you have a knack for quickly learning new, complex topics and distilling them for others.


You will:

  • Partner closely with 3-4 Account Executives, to analyse and understand customers’ businesses, climate ambitions and software needs

  • Become a trusted advisor to our prospective customers—educating them about corporate climate commitments, carbon accounting, regulation/policy and the Watershed offering

  • Build and share subject matter expertise on how the world’s largest companies can run successful climate programs

  • Demonstrate Watershed’s unique value to prospective customers, through product demonstrations, ROI analysis and customer stories

  • Creatively apply the Agentic AI capabilities of the Watershed platform to address innovative use cases

  • Scope complex customer engagements as Watershed expands to new industries

  • Interface with Customer Success and Sustainability Advisory teams to ensure smooth handovers from pre- to post-contract

  • Collaborate with Watershed’s Engineering, Product and Marketing teams to continuously improve Watershed’s products and positioning

  • It is a mandatory requirement to have business level French and German for this role

You might be a fit if you:

  • Have worked in a Solutions Consulting or Sales Engineering role for an Enterprise SaaS company

  • Have partnered with Account Executives to scope successful engagements with mid-sized to large companies

  • Master new concepts and technologies quickly

  • Have exceptional communication and presentation skills; can engage deeply with both technical and business executive audiences

  • Get energy from working across multiple projects concurrently and wearing many hats

  • Are passionate about decarbonising diverse industries, from aviation to manufacturing to cloud computing

  • Are excited to join a startup and are ready to take responsibility defining a new standard for climate and Sustainability AI programs around the world!

Considered a “very nice to have” if you:

  • Have a background in corporate climate programs or carbon accounting

Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles)

Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process.

At Watershed, we are dedicated to ensuring an inclusive recruitment process.
